newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: StanChart cleared to sell stake in S.Lanka bank.
newsitem.headline: StanChart cleared to sell stake in S.Lanka bank.

text.p: Britain's Standered Chartered (U.K.) Holdings Ltd has been allowed to sell its stake in Sri Lanka's Commercial Bank subject to certain conditions, the local bank said on Friday.

Commercial Bank said in a statement to the Colombo Stock Exchange that Sri Lanka's Central Bank has said that Standard Chartered could sell most of its 10 million voting shares, or 40 percent stake, to Hatton National Bank (HNB) and Development Finance Corporation (DFCC).
The statement said that StanChart could sell 2.5 million shares to HNB and another 6.25 million to DFCC.
It said the remaining 1.25 million shares could be sold to existing shareholders of Commercial Bank other than Hatton National and DFCC.
But the Central Bank said the sale could take place only if HNB did not end up holding more than 10 percent of the voting shares in Commercial Bank and DFCC not more than 25 percent.
The statement said the proposal had been accepted by Commercial Bank but added that it was not clear whether other parties had agreed.
Earlier this year both HNB and DFCC had offered to buy StanChart's stake in Commercial Bank after the British bank said it wanted to sell out.

The Central Bank was prompted to step in to work out a compromise formula after the bidding parties started wrangling publicly over who was the more suitable buyer. There was no immediate comment available from HNB or DFCC on Friday.
Shares in Commercial Bank were quoted at 200 rupees in late trading on Friday.
